'''''Thymus pannonicus''''', known by its common name '''Hungarian thyme''' or '''Eurasian thyme''', is a [[perennial]] [[herbaceous]] plant, distributed in central and eastern Europe and Russia. It grows over open dry meadows, grasslands, and rocks.

In Serbia, this plant species contributes to several [[xerothermous]] grass formations which develop on warm, dry [[Silicate minerals|silicate]] terrains at altitude above {{convert|160|m|ft|abbr=on}}, mostly over plains or mild slopes, on acidic soils derived from crystalline [[albite]]-[[muscovite]] [[schist]] and [[gneiss]]-like [[granite]]. In southern [[Banat]] ([[Serbia]]), the dried herb is used to make herbal tea drinks, owing to its lemon-like scent. Fresh leaves are used for aromatisation of homemade jams, candies and similar confections. Traditionally, it is used also for coughs and other respiratory complaints, as well as certain gastrointestinal disorders.<ref name=Zoran>{{cite journal | doi = 10.2478/s11535-008-0013-x| title = Chemical composition and antimicrobial activity of Thymus pannonicus All. (Lamiaceae) essential oil| journal = Open Life Sciences| volume = 3| issue = 2| year = 2008| last1 = Maksimović| first1 = Zoran| last2 = Milenković| first2 = Marina| last3 = Vučićević| first3 = Dragana| last4 = Ristić| first4 = Mihailo| pages = 149–154| doi-access = free}}</ref>

== Chemical composition ==

According to Karuza-Stojaković et al., the principal constituents of ''T. pannonicus'' [[essential oil]] from southern parts of Vojvodina province (northern Serbia) were [[terpinyl acetate]], [[terpinen-4-ol]], [[thymol]], [[carvacrol]], and [[geranyl acetate]] (listed in order of descending quantity).<ref>Ljiljana Karuza-Stojaković, Stamenko Pavlović, Predrag Živanović, Branka Todorović. Količina i sastav etarskih ulja različitih vrsta roda Thymus L., Arhiv za farmaciju, 1989, 39, 105-111 (in Serbian)</ref> Recent comprehensive studies of chemical variability in [[Hydrodistillation|hydrodistilled]] essential oils of different wild growing and cultivated populations of ''T. pannonicus'' from Hungary, as well as supercritical fluid extracts of various ''Lamiaceae'' species, confirmed that high concentrations of both thymol and [[p-cymene]] are the main chemosystematic attributes of ''T. pannonicus'' essential oil.<ref>{{cite journal | doi = 10.1300/J044v13n01_03 | title = Evaluation of Environmental Factors Influencing Essential Oil Quality of ''Thymus pannonicus'' All. and ''Thymus praecox'' Opiz | journal = Journal of Herbs, Spices & Medicinal Plants | volume = 13 | pages = 23–43 | year = 2007 | last1 = Pluhár | first1 = Zsuzsanna | last2 = Héthelyi | first2 = Éva | last3 = Kutta | first3 = Gabriella | last4 = Kamondy | first4 = Lívia | issue = 1 | bibcode = 2007JHSMP..13...23P }}</ref><ref>Kutta G., Pluhár Zs., Sárosi Sz., Yield and composition of supercritical fluid extracts of different Lamiaceae species, Int. J. Hort. Sci., 2007, 13, 79-82</ref> Further research efforts of Pluhár Zs. et al. on the volatile oil composition of ''T. pannonicus'' from nineteen different localities of Hungary, confirmed a significant essential oil polymorphism in this plant species, as twelve different chemovarieties were determined, namely: thymol, thymol/p-cymene, thymol/p-cymene/[[γ-terpinene]], thymol/p-cymene/[[neral (chemical)|neral]], thymol/p-cymene/γ-terpinene/[[β-bisabolene]], thymol/p-cymene/[[isoborneol]]/γ-terpinene, thymol/[[linalyl acetate]]/γ-terpinene/[[α-cubebene]], p-cymene/[[geraniol]]/linalyl acetate, linalyl acetate/geranyl acetate, [[germacrene D]]/[[β-caryophyllene]], [[caryophyllene oxide]]/α-cubebene/[[linalool]], and germacrene D/β-caryophyllene/[[farnesol]].<ref>{{cite journal | doi = 10.1177/1934578X1000501034 | title = Essential Oil Polymorphism of Wild Growing Hungarian Thyme (Thymus Pannonicus) Populations in the Carpathian Basin | journal = Natural Product Communications | volume = 5 | issue = 10 | pages = 1681–1686 | year = 2010 | last1 = Pluhár | first1 = Zsuzsanna | last2 = Sárosi | first2 = Szilvia | last3 = Pintér | first3 = Adrienn | last4 = Simkó | first4 = Hella | pmid = 21121273 | doi-access = free }}</ref>

On the other hand, a ''T. pannonicus'' population, which is located over the southern slopes of [[Vršac Mountains]] in southern Banat (Vojvodina province, Serbia) was characterised by exceptionally high percentage of oxygenated monoterpenes (91.75%). The most abundant components of its [[essential oil]] were identified as [[geranial]] (41.42%, w/w) and neral (29.61%, w/w), the mixture of which is frequently referred to as [[citral]].<ref name=Zoran/>

== Biological activity ==

The antimicrobial activity of essential oil was evaluated using the [[agar disc diffusion]] and [[broth microdilution]] methods against ''[[Staphylococcus aureus]]'', ''[[Enterococcus faecalis]]'', ''[[Pseudomonas aeruginosa]]'', ''[[Escherichia coli]]'', two strains of ''[[Klebsiella pneumoniae]]'' and two strains of ''[[Candida albicans]]''. The essential oil exhibited ''[[in vitro]]'' antimicrobial activity to varying degrees against all tested strains. The maximum activity of ''T. pannonicus'' oil was observed against ''E. coli'', ''S. aureus'' and both tested strains of ''C. albicans'' ([[Minimum inhibitory concentration|MIC]] = 50 μl/ml, each). Moderate activity was observed against ''P. aeruginosa'' and one of the tested strains of ''K. pneumoniae'' (MIC = 200 μl/ml), while ''E. faecalis'' and the other strain of ''K. pneumoniae'' expressed a higher degree of resistance (MIC > 200 μl/ml))<ref name=Zoran/>
